92-minor-programs: Desautels also offers minors for non-Management students that may suit this Faculty's students (p. 902).
95-program-description-2: Core science prerequisites for students coming from high school outside CEGEP.
96-program-description-2: The science entrance prerequisites for students coming from high school outside CEGEP.
96-program-description-3: Core science prerequisites for students coming from high school outside CEGEP.
100-about-the-department-of-bioresource-: Engineering applied to plants, animals and ecosystems: sustainable food and biomaterial production, and protecting soil, water and other resources. An accredited B.Eng. run with the Faculty of Engineering, focused on the circular bioeconomy.
100-about-programs-in-bioresource-engine: Accredited by the Canadian Engineering Accreditation Board, leading to professional engineer status in any province. The Professional Agrology version also qualifies you for the Ordre des agronomes.

Three non-restrictive streams: Bio-Environmental (soil and water, waste, ecology, climate), Bio-Production (machines, instrumentation, geospatial data, precision agriculture), Bio-Process (food, fibre, fuel and biochemical products). An Honours program and minors are also available.

Mostly on the Macdonald Campus, with one term downtown. Minors include Agribusiness Entrepreneurship, Agricultural Production, Biomedical Engineering, Biotechnology, Computer Science, Construction Management, Environmental Engineering, Field Studies and Technological Entrepreneurship.

C minimum in required and complementary courses. 143 credits include 30 from U0, with at least 50% at McGill. Required courses must be at McGill, with rare exceptions, and the capstone BREE 490/495 must be done in the Department.
101-program-description: Engineering for biological, agricultural, food and environmental systems, including bio-based products, with a research focus. Graduates can register as engineers in any province and some other countries.
101-set-c-social-sciences: Plus 6 credits of social sciences, management, humanities or law at U1 or higher with adviser approval, which may include one 3-credit course in a language you don't normally speak. ENVR courses have limited enrolment.
102-set-d-engineering: Up to 6 of these may come from other Engineering courses with adviser approval.
103-program-description: The engineering degree above, with registration as an engineer plus eligibility for the Ordre des agronomes and similar bodies in other provinces.
104-set-d-engineering: At least 6 from each group. With approval, 6 may come from other Engineering courses.
106-about-the-farm-management-and-techno: A three-year college program in commercial agriculture at Macdonald: soil, plants, animals, engineering and management, with internships.
106-academic-rules-and-information: McGill's rules and Québec's Ministry rules for the college level both apply.
106-entrance-requirements: Practical farming knowledge for eastern Canada: a year's experience recommended, or a four-month summer in special cases.
Québec: SSD plus Secondary IV History, Science and Technology, Mathematics, and Secondary V Language of Instruction and Second Language.

Ontario: OSSD plus grade 10 French, science SNC2P or SNC2D (with a tech course), and math MFM2P or MPM2D. Other Canadians need grade 10 second-language French. International students may need French and English tests.
Everyone comes for an interview. Fall admission only. Get car and farm equipment licences first, for safety and because employers require them.
106-sessional-dates: Set by the Ministry, currently 75 teaching days and seven exam days per semester.
106-registration: Register in Minerva each semester. Courses normally won't run with fewer than five students.
106-academic-standing: First semester: failing half or more courses, or averaging below 60%, means withdrawing for at least a semester, then applying in writing to the Director.
Later: a cumulative or semester average under 60%, or failing half or more, means probation, possibly limited to 10 credits with course approval by the Associate Director.
Two probationary semesters in a row means withdrawing, with readmission possible after 6 to 12 months, on probation.
107-student-rights-and-responsibilities: See the Secretariat's Policies and Regulations site.
107-institutional-policy-on-the-evaluati: Explains how learning is evaluated, who's responsible for what, and how standards are accounted for. Copies are in the Library.
107-fees: No tuition for eligible Québec residents, thanks to the provincial agriculture ministry. Full-time out-of-province and international students pay tuition, and part-time (under 8 credits) pays half. Everyone pays student fees. Rates are on Student Accounts.
107-financial-assistance: Need-based loans and bursaries for full-time students, after applying for maximum government aid. Apply in Minerva and meet a counsellor at Student Services, Macdonald.
107-residence-accommodation: Laird Hall: co-ed, 250 students, double and single rooms, with shared washrooms, kitchen, lounge and laundry on each floor.
107-program-description: Three years, funded by the provincial agriculture ministry, aiming for professional competence, mobility and lifelong learning.
107-program-overview: Six terms on campus. Year 1's first summer is a 13-week internship on another farm or agricultural business, prepared through two Stage courses. Year 2's summer is Enterprise Management 1, collecting data for later courses.
English, Français, Humanities, Physical Education and two complementaries lead to the DEC.
108-fall-2: Two from the elective production list.
108-elective-production-courses: Four animal and four plant science courses. Take at least two from each, four in all, and at least two a semester. More is possible with your adviser.
109-complementary-courses: Take two. With your adviser, you can substitute courses from another college at your own cost, including science courses for further study.
109-comprehensive-assessment: Mandatory for the DEC; pass at 60%. It's noted on your transcript.
109-english-exit-examination: Required for the DEC, set by the Ministry on its dates.
110-about-the-department-of-food-science: Chemistry, physics, biology, engineering and microbiology applied to food quality and safety, covering analytical chemistry, risk assessment, product development, packaging, processing, flavour and sensory science.

Accredited by the Institute of Food Technologists and recognized by CIFST. Offers the B.Sc. (Food Chemistry or Food Science option), a concurrent B.Sc. with Nutritional Sciences, and a post-baccalaureate Certificate.
110-concurrent-bachelor-of-science-in-fo: Two degrees together, unique in North America. Food Science covers chemistry, safety, processing and packaging, and Nutritional Science covers metabolism and nutrition, with an industry placement.
110-program-description: Food processing, chemistry, quality assurance, analysis, products and regulations, for scientist roles in industry or government.
Qualifies you for CIFST, and possibly IFT and the Ordre des chimistes. Reaches 90 credits with free electives. See Minimum Credit Requirements for prerequisites.
111-required-courses-54-credits: Without a CEGEP organic chemistry course, FDSC 230 must be taken in its place.
111-additional-required-courses-food-che: Qualifies you for IFT and Ordre des chimistes recognition.
111-electives-6-credits: Choose with an adviser to reach 90 credits, partly in humanities or social sciences.
111-program-description: Combines both fields to develop healthy foods, integrating both degrees' requirements and professional or industry training.

Honours: 12 extra credits beyond major and specialization. Apply in March or April of U3 with a CGPA of 3.3, once a professor agrees to supervise. Earn B or higher in Honours courses and a 3.3 CGPA at graduation. Your Program Director, supervisor and you sign a description of the research.
112-honours-plan-a: Two 6-credit research courses in your major's area, chosen with the Program Director and supervisor.
112-honours-plan-b: At least two 3-credit Honours courses and 6 credits at the 400 or 500 level in the Faculty, on a topic related to your major, chosen with the Program Director and supervisor.
113-program-description: Combines food science and nutrition to develop healthy foods, satisfying both degrees and including professional or industry training.
114-elective-courses-12-credits: Choose with an adviser. Not all courses run every year.
115-program-description: The Food Science option with research. Apply in March or April of U2 with a CGPA of 3.3 and a supervisor; earn B or higher in the 12 Honours credits and 3.3 at graduation.
Food processing, chemistry, quality and regulations, for scientist roles. Qualifies you for CIFST and possibly IFT. Reaches 90 credits with electives.
116-program-description: For mature students with a science-related degree, as a way into food industries or graduate food science. One core course, then complementaries in chemistry and analysis, microbiology and nutrition, quality and safety, processing, communication and ethics.
118-about-the-school-of-human-nutrition: Part of McGill's Health Sciences, focused on food choices, metabolism and health.

Dietetics Major: 3.5 years, 115 credits, accredited, leading to registration as a dietitian (ODNQ in Québec, where the titles are reserved). 1,500 unpaid Stage hours at four levels in clinical, community and food service settings.

Nutrition Major: 90 credits, with four concentrations, plus research, field studies or a minor. No licensure, but good preparation for graduate and professional schools, industry, government, NGOs and global health.
Dual B.Sc. in Food Science and Nutritional Science: 122 credits. See Undergraduate Admissions to apply.
118-bachelor-of-science-in-nutritional-s: Dietetics (professional) or Nutrition, with concentrations in Food Function and Safety, Global Nutrition, Metabolism, Health and Disease, or Sports Nutrition.
118-m-sc-a-m-sc-and-ph-d: Master's by thesis or not, and a thesis Ph.D. M.Sc. (Applied) options: Dietetics Credentialing, Practicum, Project.
118-academic-standing: General rules on p. 88. Dietetics: Stage courses require a CGPA of at least 3.00, firmly applied. Below 3.0 for two consecutive years means you can't continue.
119-program-description: Competency-based, 3.5 years, on food and nutrition, leadership, communication, management and critical thinking. 40 weeks of Stage in clinical, public health and food provision settings. Accredited; graduates may register as dietitians in any province.
119-required-courses-112-credits: Courses and Stages follow a set order over nine terms; see the School's program plan.
119-compulsory-immunization: Required, completed when starting Year 1 and confirmed by the Student Wellness Hub. Deadlines apply.
119-program-description-2: Concentrated research in Human Nutrition. Nutrition Major students with CGPA 3.6+ and A- or higher in all NUTR courses can apply to transfer in Winter U2, after finding a supervisor.
Graduate with 90+ credits, keeping both standards; otherwise, you can move back to the Major.
